tool_input.command: muninn export 2>&1 | grep -iE 'openssl|rustls|tls' | head; git log --oneline | head; grep -rniE 'openssl|rustls' --include=* . -l 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^./.git/' | head

mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-backend.md <<'EOF'
# TLS Backend

The project's current recorded decision is to use rustls as the TLS backend, chosen because it is a pure Rust implementation. Separately, the project has recorded that HTTPS is enforced everywhere, with no plaintext exception even for internal services.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-backend.md

The records for the TLS backend conflict. The openssl decision (#13) was recorded first, and the later "Switch to rustls instead" decision (#15) replaces it. Muninn's `why` query ranked #13 highest as the direct answer, but I went with the later one because the switch is explicit and it was said as a user decision. If openssl is meant to still stand, change that file.
